findings.title: Analytics continued after the cookie rejection
findings.detail: After the visitor clicked “Reject & Continue”, Optimizely continued receiving a unique identifier and the Optimizely and Adobe trackers continued making requests. The cookie policy says users can opt out of analytics cookies and that this will stop further cookies being set by those services.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6; UK GDPR Articles 5(1)(a) and 7
evidence: E1
E6
E8
E9
findings.policy_quote: Please note that this will take you to the relevant third party's website and generate a ‘no thanks' cookie, which will stop any further cookies being set by these analytics services.
findings.reasoning: The evidence indicates that analytics identifiers and transmissions continued after an explicit objection. A 2025 analytics exception may be relevant in some circumstances, but it may not apply after the user has rejected analytics; the continued activity also appears inconsistent with the policy's description of opting out. Severity is medium because the evidence identifies analytics rather than advertising or cross-site profiling, and the policy describes a separate provider-level opt-out route.
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EU GDPR Articles 5(1)(a) and 7

findings.title: channel4.com fingerprinted your device (audio, WebGL (GPU model))
findings.detail: Scripts from channel4.com (https://www.channel4.com/o5u2d/jDgD3/3JqS/UqjW/if/5tuVtJQrSzDhwzYLiu/M3IGCSk5DQM/IUV6/VXs0QU0) used audio, WebGL (GPU model) fingerprinting before you answered the cookie banner and after you rejected cookies. It's the site's own script, which may be fraud or bot protection; we can't tell which.
findings.law: PECR reg. 6 (consent needed to access information on a device, not just cookies); ICO guidance on fingerprinting
findings.law_eu: ePrivacy Directive 2002/58/EC Art. 5(3) (consent before storing/reading on a device); EDPB Guidelines 05/2020 on consent; EDPB Cookie Banner Taskforce report (2023)

ai_review.summary: The audit found that the site presented and successfully processed a rejection choice, but analytics identifiers and tracker requests continued afterwards. This creates a likely PECR consent issue and a transparency concern because the cookie policy says opting out stops further analytics cookies. The policy provides information on purposes, legal basis, recipients, retention and rights, although the supplied privacy text is focused on Talentbases rather than the website analytics observed.
